spec: Build a to-do list REST API. Users can add tasks, list tasks, mark a task as completed, and delete tasks. Each task has a description, a due date and a completed flag. Tasks are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: Single DynamoDB-backed task entity with a small CRUD surface.

congruence_checklist: Task model has description, due date, completed flag

plan.summary: A FastAPI REST service for managing to-do tasks. Clients (web/mobile front-ends or scripts) can create tasks with a description and due date, list all tasks, mark an individual task as completed, and delete tasks. All task records persist in a single DynamoDB table that the service accesses directly with boto3.

endpoints.purpose: Create a new task from a JSON body containing description and due_date; generates a task_id, sets completed=false, stores the item in DynamoDB and returns the created task.
List all tasks via a DynamoDB scan, with an optional completed=true/false query filter.
Retrieve a single task by its id; returns 404 if it does not exist.
Mark the specified task as completed (sets completed=true and completed_at) and return the updated task.
Update mutable fields of a task (description, due_date, completed) and return the updated task.
Delete the specified task from DynamoDB; returns 404 if the task does not exist.
Liveness/readiness probe used by the evaluation harness; reports service status and DynamoDB table reachability.

data_models.name: Task
fields: completed_at: str | None (ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, set when marked complete)

aws_resources.name: tasks
aws_resources.justification: Primary persistence for task records as required by the spec ('Tasks are stored in DynamoDB'). Partition key task_id (String), PAY_PER_REQUEST billing; read/written directly by the FastAPI service on every endpoint.

aws_resources.name: todo_api_app_role
aws_resources.justification: Role/policy granting the backend service least-privilege access (GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, Scan, DescribeTable) to the tasks table only.

assumptions: No authentication or multi-user separation was specified, so the API is unauthenticated and all tasks live in a single shared namespace (no user_id partitioning).
Task ids are server-generated UUID4 strings rather than client-supplied.
due_date is stored as an ISO-8601 date string (YYYY-MM-DD) and validated on input; times of day are out of scope.
Listing uses a DynamoDB Scan because task volume is expected to be small; no secondary indexes or pagination cursors are planned beyond an optional completed filter.
'Mark a task as completed' is exposed as a dedicated PATCH /tasks/{task_id}/complete endpoint, plus a general PATCH for other field updates.

No queueing, notification, file upload, scheduling or secret storage is implied, so SQS, SNS, S3, Lambda, API Gateway and Secrets Manager are intentionally omitted; the service runs locally and calls DynamoDB directly.
CloudWatch is not provisioned as a separate resource since the app logs to stdout and no Lambda functions exist to emit metrics.
DynamoDB endpoint, region and table name are supplied via environment variables (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_REGION, TASKS_TABLE) for LocalStack compatibility.
